full_judgment:
11. Heard the learned advocates for the contending, parties, perused the writ petition, supplementary affidavit" affidavit-in-opposition, annexures appended thereto and the law referred to by both the parties. Regarding the issue involved in this Rule, we requested Mr Sayed Shahid Hossain, the learned advocate of this Court, to assist us. Accordingly, referring to section 2(Ka)(18) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 he contends that all financial institution has every right to file suits before the Artha Rin Adalat for realization of any debt and the Letter of Credit (L/C) being a "Rinpatra" and in the present case the same being issued in favour of the borrower which has been presented by M/s MBA Trade & Commerce to the Jamuna Bank Limited who having purchased the said' bill, the said transaction has become a contract between the Jamuna Bank and the Sonali Bank i.e, the negotiating bank and the issuer bank respectively. As such the provision of section 2(ga)(1) of the Ain comes into operation. Thus the suit instituted by the Jamuna Bank against Sonali Bank only is very much maintainable. Mr Hossain further contended that in the present case it is not at all necessary to look for whether there is any borrower, because M/s MBA Trade and Commerce being the beneficiary of the Letter of Credit (L/C) placed the same before the Jamuna Bank and got the money. from the Jamuna Bank .and the Jamuna Sank having sent the Letter of Credit (L/C) to the L/C Issuing bank i.e. Sonali Bank, who is the custodian of the same under the Banking Law is liable to pay the L/C amount. Having not done so the Sonali Bank has been rightly sued, as such, it is liable to pay the L/C money. Hence the provision of section 6(5) of the Ain will not protect the Sonali Bank under the facts and circumstances of the case. In this respect he referred to Paragraph 8 of the case of Uttara Bank vs Macneill & Kilburn Ltd, reported in 1981 BLD (AD) 230 = 33 DLR (AD) 298, To make the entire case clear Mr Hossain contended that the borrower is a person who borrows from someone and debtor is a person who indebted something to do. Here the Sonali Bank having opened the Letter of Credit it has indebted itself to pay the money of the Lie value to the person Or institution or the authority who wanted to negotiate the same. So under such circumstances institution of the suit against the Sonali Bank only is wholly in accordance with law and the suit is not barred for non joinder of necessary parties or misjoinder of improper parties under Order VII, rule 11 (a) and (d) of the Code of Civil Procedure. In addition to his above submissions he contended that the principle of law in deciding, a case whether the same is barred by law is wholly dependable on the facts and circumstances of the statements in the plaint. 

 17. At this stage, Mr Khan upon reiterating his contentions submits that M/s MBA Trade and Commerce having borrowed money from Jamuna Bank against the bill arising out of L/C, he is a borrower and without making him a party in the suit the said suit is barred for defect of non- joinder of necessary party and misjoinder of improper party and the same is barred by Section 6(5) of the Ain. As such the plaint should be rejected and hence the rejection of his application by the impugned order of this writ petition on the face of section 6(5) is illegal. The question, as to whether M/s MBA Trade and Commerce is a borrower or not, can very well be agitated before the trial court. As such his contention has no legal basis.
